steps.label: Identify a, b, c and find √(a²+b²)
steps.margin_note: First mark. The sine coefficient is −24 and the cosine one is 7. Both get squared, so both signs disappear.
steps.memory_tip: The sine coefficient is −24 and the cosine one is 7. Both get squared, so both signs disappear.
lines: Comparing with a sinx + b cosx + c:

accept: a is minus twenty four b is seven c is five and the root of five seventy six plus forty nine is twenty five
identify the coefficients and get twenty five
root six twenty five is twenty five
a minus twenty four, b seven, c five, root twenty five

steps.why: 7, 24, 25 is a Pythagorean triple, which is why the root comes out whole. Recognising it saves a long square root.
common_mistakes: Taking √(a² + b²) as a + b, giving 31 instead of 25.

steps.label: Write the range as an interval
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Compute both ends, then write them as [minimum, maximum] — smallest first, which is the convention for an interval.
steps.memory_tip: Write the interval smallest first: [minimum, maximum] = [−20, 30].

recall.must_convey: That the range is written as the interval [−20, 30], minimum first.
accept: maximum thirty and minimum minus twenty so the range is minus twenty to thirty
write it as the closed interval minus twenty comma thirty
the range is from minus twenty to thirty
range minus twenty to thirty ani rasta
the interval is minus twenty to thirty

steps.why: The expression takes every value between its two extremes, so the range is a closed interval — not just the two endpoints listed.
common_mistakes: Writing the interval the wrong way round as [30, −20].
Giving only the two numbers without interval notation.

insider_note: Range, not just maximum and minimum, so the answer must be written as the interval [−20, 30]. The +5 shifts both ends, and 7 with 24 give the Pythagorean 25.
